title: No partiality (Acts 10:34–48)
hook: Peter opens his mouth in a stranger's house and admits he's just learned something
tomorrow: who gave the believers their name? Acts leaves a blank.

segments.voice: Yesterday, a sheet let down three times, and Peter learning to call no one common or unclean. The line: what god has cleansed.

I see it now. I didn't before. Sentences like that only come after you've been wrong for a while. Peter is standing in a Gentile's house in Caesarea. The room is full of Cornelius' relatives and close friends, all of them waiting to hear him. He opens his mouth, and the first thing he says is something he has only just learned: "Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons." I perceive. Not, I have always known. He says it as a discovery, made somewhere between a rooftop in Joppa and this doorway. Then he starts to preach, and partway through, something interrupts him.
screen: `I SEE IT NOW.` → `A ROOM FULL OF GENTILES.` → `I PERCEIVE.`

segments.voice: Respecter of persons is older English for someone who plays favorites, who judges by face, rank or nation. Peter goes on: "But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him." Every nation. Then he tells the story of Jesus of Nazareth, short and plain: a man "who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil," the cross, the third day, witnesses who ate and drank with him after he rose. And then the interruption. "While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word." The sermon isn't finished. The Spirit doesn't wait for it to be. That's the detail to tell a friend tonight: in this story, God doesn't let the preacher get to the end. The believers who came with Peter are astonished, "because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost." And Peter asks: "Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?" On the desert road, the traveler from Ethiopia asked almost the same question: what doth hinder me? Here Peter answers it for a whole household. They're baptized, and the scene ends with an invitation: they ask him to stay a few days.
screen: `NO RESPECTER OF PERSONS.` · `IN EVERY NATION.` · `THE SPIRIT INTERRUPTS THE SERMON.` · `CAN ANY MAN FORBID WATER?` · then, large: `NO RESPECTER OF PERSONS.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and paper and write three names: someone you admire, someone you barely notice, someone you find hard. Under each name, write the same short good wish, word for word. Then sit with the page, and look at the three names side by side.
No partiality. Peter's discovery in Cornelius' house: God is no respecter of persons.
Hold onto this: no respecter of persons, a thing Peter perceived, not a thing he'd always known. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians come back to Peter's words, God is no respecter of persons, when they talk about welcoming people of every nation and background.

myth: Peter says he had always known God plays no favorites
he says, I perceive: a discovery, made after the rooftop vision.
the Spirit fell before Peter finished speaking
while Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard.
Cornelius' household was baptized first, then received the Spirit
here it's the other way round: the Spirit fell, then Peter asked, can any man forbid water?

fork.setup: your team captain gives the best drills to her friends, and you're one of her friends. what does Peter's discovery ask of you?
options: say something, even though the favoritism helps you.
enjoy it; favorites are only wrong when you're left out.
wait until someone who's left out complains first.
fork.reveal: God is no respecter of persons, in every nation. Peter learned it in a house where he was the insider, and changed how he acted there.

original.note: Greek: respecter of persons, one who shows partiality; Acts 10:34.

trapdoor: what you thought: no partiality is just about being fair.
what it means: Peter's discovery that God accepts people in every nation, followed by the Spirit falling on a Gentile household.
what a scholar hears: Acts 10:47 echoes 8:36: can any man forbid water, and what doth hinder me. the same question, answered twice.
guess: a judge's duty to rule without bias in court
staying neutral in an argument between friends
recall: a sheet let down three times

chat.says: ok nia's obviously welcome. but do i have to be nice to KAYLA now too? she started all this.
options: No favorites cuts both ways: the welcome you want for Nia, Kayla gets too.
Not yet. Peter only welcomed Cornelius after he proved he was devout.
Just be polite. Partiality is about strangers, not people who hurt you.
chat.meaning: Peter perceived that God is no respecter of persons: in every nation, accepted. The same welcome, without picking favorites.

Gentile.meaning: a person who is not Jewish

Caesarea.meaning: the coastal city where Cornelius lived

respecter of persons.meaning: older English for someone who plays favorites

Nazareth.meaning: the town in Galilee where Jesus grew up
